The pre-existing tests/platform/windows/package-channels.test.mjs (2/2, committed in 199d790f, not modified by this task) was also re-run and still passes, confirming this task's additions did not disturb the pre-existing internal windows-channels contract or its validator.
observed: This task adds the generator/validator pipeline that turns RightKit's real, already-signed Windows artifact into the two real channel manifest formats, and proves it deterministically: scripts/release/channels/right-release-source.mjs reads & independently re-verifies RightKit's sealed .right-release/sealed/<app>-<version>-<commit8>/windows/release-manifest.json (schema, checkpoints through 'sealed', on-disk file hash/size) and derives version/commit/installer-name/SHA-256/public-URL from it, using the same PUBLIC_DOWNLOAD_BASE constant RightKit's own pub-upload.mjs uses -- never an invented value -- and fails closed as a declared gap if more than one installer artifact or a non-x64 name is ever sealed (this app ships x64 only today). scripts/release/channels/generate-windows-channels.mjs combines that real artifact with a validated MBR-902 clean-machine receipt (reusing ../windows/contract.mjs#validateReceipt and ../verify-windows-channels.mjs#verifyWindowsChannels unmodified) and, only once both are proven, builds the real WinGet 3-file YAML manifest (winget-manifest.mjs: InstallerType nsis, Architecture x64, InstallerSwitches Silent/SilentWithProgress '/S', UpgradeBehavior install for version detection) and the real Scoop bucket manifest fields (scoop-manifest.mjs: architecture.64bit.installer/uninstaller '/S', checkver/autoupdate) -- validating both before ever writing a file. Run directly against this actual checkout, generateWindowsChannels correctly reports 'unavailable' with named reasons (no sealed release exists yet; only mac releases are sealed today) and writes nothing, matching the pre-existing packaging/winget/release.v1.json and packaging/scoop/membrane.json which remain untouched and still state=unavailable/publish=false. The packaging/winget/manifests/o/Orthic/Membrane/UNAVAILABLE/ trio is the real, install-format WinGet manifest that was missing before this task; it is intentionally invalid (PackageVersion '0.0.0-unavailable', InstallerUrl/InstallerSha256 declared UNAVAILABLE sentinels) and is asserted to fail the same validateWingetManifests a real winget-pkgs manifest check would apply.
gap: Actually running `winget install`/`upgrade`/`uninstall` and `scoop install`/`update`/`uninstall` against the real installer on a clean Windows machine requires: (1) a real RightKit-sealed & Azure-Artifact-Signed Windows release (`pnpm --dir apps/membrane-hub run release:build:win`, out of scope here -- no build/sign command was run), and (2) the MBR-902/MBR-806 clean-machine install/update/uninstall receipt for that exact sealed hash. Neither exists on this checkout yet (only macOS releases are sealed under .right-release/sealed/). Per this task's hard rules and MEMBRANE-BOOK-MODE-EXECUTION-RULES.md, that credentialed, clean-machine run is AWAITING_CREDENTIALLED_RUN and is deferred to the Book 3 final phased gate, which is the only place `node scripts/release/verify-release-plan.mjs --task MBR-905` and any right-release/winget/scoop/signtool command may run. This task ships the generator/validator pipeline that lets that later run produce real, verifiable manifests from RightKit's real output; it does not claim the run itself happened, and status is recorded as pending_book_gate, not pass.
